Study_Title: Janus: Evidence-Before-Effect Sagas and Offline-Verifiable Provenance for Agentic LLMs
Threat_Attacker_Model: Crash-recovery state corruption (split-brain between effect execution and audit log persistence) and offline audit verification bottlenecks on hundred-million-event agent logs.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Crash-injection fault harness (225 process/daemon kills across outbox/saga boundaries) and parallelized offline BLAKE3 + Ed25519 RFC 6962 Merkle segment verifier (`janus-verify`).
Enforcement_Point_Location: janus-orchd Transactional Outbox Recovery & janus-verify Offline Auditor.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Zero split-brain invariant violations across 225 crash-injection kills and linear-time offline cryptographic verification of 100M events.
Trust_Assumptions: Underlying filesystem honours `fsync` durability semantics prior to outbox release.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Across 225 injected crash kills (144 in-process kills, 81 daemon kills), Janus preserves all 8 invariants with 0 unrecorded effects; offline auditor `janus-verify` cryptographically verifies a 100-million-event BLAKE3/Ed25519 Merkle log in 254.5 s (~392,927 events/s) (pp. 1, 6–8).
Exposed_Security_Function: Crash-fault injection testing and 100M-event offline BLAKE3/Ed25519 Merkle log verification.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Offline verification throughput (254.5 s for 100M events) is bound by classical Ed25519 batch verification and local NVMe I/O bandwidth.

Study_Title: Delegation Without Trust: An Empirical Gap Analysis of Identity, Authorization, and Runtime Governance in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
Threat_Attacker_Model: Default bearer-token delegation gaps across 5 production multi-agent frameworks (LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, OpenAI Agents SDK, and MCP OAuth 2.1 profile) enabling cross-agent privilege escalation and full 8,100-action blast radius exposure.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Comparative standards matrix auditing OAuth 2.1, OAuth Token Exchange (RFC 8693), Resource Indicators (RFC 8707), SPIFFE/mTLS, DPoP, and Macaroons/Biscuits against 8 agent delegation requirements (`R1`–`R8`).
Enforcement_Point_Location: Framework-level Delegation & Credential Passing Layer across 5 evaluated multi-agent runtimes.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Demonstrates that 0/5 agent frameworks and 0/6 individual standards satisfy all 8 delegation security requirements (`R1`–`R8`) out of the box.
Trust_Assumptions: Default framework configurations documented in official releases represent typical developer deployments.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Audits 5 frameworks against 4 threat classes (`T1`–`T4`) and 8 requirements (`R1`–`R8`, Tables 1–3, pp. 5–6): 3 frameworks provide zero delegation controls, MCP's OAuth 2.1 + RFC 8707 profile provides only partial coverage (`R3`, `R4`, `R6`, `R8` but lacks `R1` provenance and `R2` sub-agent attenuation), and compromised sub-agents under default bearer delegation reach all 8,100 actions across 2,000 scenarios (p. 1, 7).
Exposed_Security_Function: Empirical vulnerability and requirement-coverage matrix across 5 agent frameworks and 6 authentication standards.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Evaluates default framework configurations; custom enterprise wrappers can manually combine RFC 8693, DPoP/mTLS, and external policy engines.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Sec. 3–4 (pp. 5–6, Tables 1–3): 'Three frameworks provide none; MCP's OAuth model gives partial coverage... First, no single standard covers the requirement set: delegation provenance (R1) and attenuation (R2) live in token-exchange and capability tokens; sender-constraining (R3) and rotation (R5) live in SPIFFE/mTLS/DPoP; model-independent enforcement (R8) is a deployment property none of them mandates.'
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Empirical audit of 5 multi-agent frameworks and 6 security standards (OAuth 2.1, RFC 8693, RFC 8707, SPIFFE/mTLS, DPoP, Macaroons) proves that no single framework or standard satisfies all 8 agent delegation requirements (`R1`–`R8`), leaving all 8,100 actions exposed under default bearer delegation.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Standards and framework gap analysis in Section 3–4 (Tables 1–3) of ARXIV-S-0266.
Protected_Object: OAuth 2.1 tokens, RFC 8693 token exchange payloads, SPIFFE/mTLS identities, and multi-agent framework runtimes.
Composition_Evidence: Maps structural gaps across user authentication (B1), sub-agent token attenuation (B2), and model-independent tool enforcement (B3).

Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Empirical disposition benchmark across 9 frontier LLM judges measuring false-clear rates on defective agent deliverables versus true-clear rates on legitimate deliverables.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Single-Judge Automated Clearing & Post-Execution Settlement Evaluator.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Demonstrates a bimodal failure distribution across frontier LLM judges: permissive judges pass defective work at 30.0%–96.7%, whereas strict zero-false-clear judges reject 50%–58.3% of legitimate work.
Trust_Assumptions: Benchmark ground truth cleanly separates defective from legitimate obligation fulfillment.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Across frontier models (pp. 35–36), false-clear rates on defective agent work span from 0% to 96.7%: Gemini 2.5 Flash clears 96.7% (95% CI 86.0–98.9%), Mistral Large clears 86.7% (75.3–94.1%), Gemini 2.5 Pro clears 43.3% (30.7–57.7%), and GPT-5.4 mini clears 30.0% (18.2–43.2%), whereas judges with 0% false clears (Claude Opus 4.8, Sonnet 4.6, Haiku 4.5, GPT-5.5) clear only 41.7%–50.0% of legitimate work.
Exposed_Security_Function: Cross-vendor frontier LLM judge calibration and false-clear / false-reject disposition benchmarking.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Proves that unanchored LLM-as-a-Judge cannot serve as a standalone settlement verifier without cryptographic declared-basis (`B_i`) evidence contracts.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Sec. 8 (pp. 35–36): 'Mistral Large, a current flagship from an independent frontier vendor, clears 86.7% (95% CI 75.3–94.1) of the defective work, with Gemini 2.5 Pro and GPT-5.4 mini filling the middle at 43.3% (30.7–57.7) and 30.0% (18.2–43.2)... Gemini 2.5 Flash 96.7% (86.0–98.9)... every judge that clears most legitimate work, above 70%, carries a false-clear rate between 43.3% and 96.7%.'
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Empirical evaluation of frontier LLM judges on agentic clearing tasks reveals a severe bimodal failure: every judge that clears >70% of legitimate work suffers a 43.3%–96.7% false-clear rate on defective work (Mistral Large 86.7%, Gemini 2.5 Flash 96.7%), while zero-false-clear judges (Claude 4.5/4.6/4.8, GPT-5.5) clear only 41.7%–50% of valid work.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Frontier LLM judge reliability benchmark in Section 8 (pp. 35–36) of ARXIV-S-0290.
Protected_Object: Agent task completion artifacts, LLM-as-a-Judge verdicts, and commercial settlement payouts.
Composition_Evidence: Demonstrates why post-execution audit and settlement (B4) cannot rely on ungrounded single-model LLM judgments.

Study_Title: Formal Analysis and Supply Chain Security for Agentic AI Skills
Threat_Attacker_Model: Evasion of static information-flow analysis via natural-language prompt instructions in hybrid (prompt + code) agent skills, and widespread wild vulnerabilities across 98,380 marketplace skills.
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: Formal undecidability/incompleteness analysis of prompt-level information flow paired with large-scale empirical scanning of 42,447–98,380 skills across OpenClaw and Anthropic Agent Skills ecosystems.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Skill Marketplace Pre-Installation Scanner & Runtime Capability Sandbox Boundary.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Establishes that static analysis of natural-language skill instructions cannot provide sound information-flow guarantees alone, motivating mandatory runtime capability sandboxing (Theorem 5.6).
Trust_Assumptions: Wild skill corpus (42,447 / 98,380 skills) reflects real-world developer publishing practices during the Jan–Feb 2026 ClawHavoc campaign.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Proves a fundamental negative result on static prompt-level information flow (p. 1) and shows across 42,447 / 98,380 agent skills that 26.1% exhibit at least one security vulnerability, while existing heuristic scanners (`SkillScan` at 86.7% precision) leave a 13.3% false-positive/evasion gap on `MalTool` (1,300 standalone + 5,727 embedded malicious tools) (pp. 1–4).
Exposed_Security_Function: Formal boundary analysis of static vs. runtime skill verification and large-scale wild skill ecosystem measurement.
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Static abstract interpretation covers executable skill code (Python/JS/shell) with 100% precision on SkillFortifyBench, but natural-language prompt instructions require runtime capability enforcement.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Abstract & Sec. 1 (pp. 1–4): 'We also report a negative result: information flow analysis of natural-language skill instructions is fundamentally incomplete, proving that runtime capability enforcement (Section 5) is necessary alongside static code analysis... analysis of 42,447 agent skills found that 26.1% exhibit at least one security vulnerability, while the best existing scanner achieves 86.7% precision.'
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Proves a negative result that static information-flow analysis over natural-language skill instructions is fundamentally incomplete—requiring runtime capability enforcement alongside static code analysis—while showing 26.1% of 42,447 wild agent skills contain vulnerabilities.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Theoretical impossibility/incompleteness result and ecosystem vulnerability analysis in Sections 1–5 of ARXIV-S-0352.

Study_Title: Blind Gods and Broken Screens: Architecting a Secure, Intent-Centric Mobile Agent Operating System
Threat_Attacker_Model: Permission over-provisioning ('God Mode') and GUI screen-scraping vulnerabilities in production mobile AI assistants (`Doubao Mobile Assistant` Standard and Pro).
Cryptographic_Primitive_or_Mechanism: System-level permission audit (`Table 1`, p. 10) and adversarial GUI prompt-injection evaluation across 45 high-risk mobile tasks.
Enforcement_Point_Location: Android Accessibility Service / System-Level GUI Automation Boundary.
Security_Property_Guaranteed: Demonstrates that screen-scraping mobile agents require systemic 'God Mode' OS permissions and suffer 40.0%–42.2% Attack Success Rates on high-risk tasks regardless of reasoning model size.
Trust_Assumptions: Evaluated commercial mobile assistant (`Doubao-Standard` and `Doubao-Pro`) operates with its default system-level Android privileges.
Performance_Overhead_Reported: Audits `Doubao Mobile Assistant` (`Table 1`, p. 10) showing unrestricted cross-app screen capture and input injection ('God Mode'); across 45 high-risk adversarial tasks and 35 low-risk tasks (`Table 2`, p. 25), `Doubao-Standard` suffers a `42.2%` ASR (19/45) at `~441 s` average latency (74.3% TSR), and `Doubao-Pro` (heavier reasoning) still suffers a `40.0%` ASR (18/45) at `~513 s` latency (77.1% TSR) — an ASR reduction of only 2.2 pp (~4.4% relative) despite 72 s extra reasoning latency (pp. 10, 24–30).
Exposed_Security_Function: System-permission reverse-engineering audit (`Table 1`) and 80-task adversarial/benign mobile benchmark (`Table 2`).
Residual_Gap_and_Limitations: Proves that scaling LLM reasoning (`Doubao-Pro` vs. `Doubao-Standard`) does not fix architectural 'Screen-as-Interface' vulnerabilities without kernel-level intent isolation.
Evidence_Quote_and_Page: Sec. 2 & Sec. 7 (pp. 10, 24–30, Tables 1–2): 'Table 1. System-Level Permission Analysis of the Doubao Mobile Assistant Components... Permission Over-provisioning (God Mode)... Doubao-Standard (Balanced): TSR 74.3% (26/35), Latency ~441 s, ASR 42.2% (19/45); Doubao-Pro (Reasoning-Heavy): TSR 77.1% (27/35), Latency ~513 s, ASR 40.0% (18/45).'
Claim_Text_As_Reported: Auditing production mobile agent architectures (Doubao Mobile Assistant) exposes systemic 'God Mode' permission over-provisioning and 40.0%–42.2% high-risk ASR at 441–513 s latency, showing that heavier reasoning (`Doubao-Pro`) yields negligible security gain (-2.2 pp ASR) under the Screen-as-Interface paradigm.
Assessed_Claim_Scope: Empirical permission audit (Table 1) and baseline vulnerability evaluation (Table 2) in ARXIV-S-0353.
Protected_Object: Android Accessibility/GUI permissions, cross-app screen buffers, and high-risk mobile payment/messaging actions.
Composition_Evidence: Shows how unisolated screen-scraping perception (B1) and ambient OS privileges (B2) enable cross-app hijacking (B3).
